items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: Austin Powell, we had the band together. And that was seven days a week, three shows a night

ctx.x: Who was in the band down there?

Horace Silvers (sic) and John Acee and Kelly Martin, at different times, and Kalil. It was a trio, no bass. And so I got tired of that and so Timmy says, "Come on." So then he showed me another new world, "the boards", they call 'em, the stage. And we rehearsed and then we went out on the road and I think our first job was in Cafe Society, together. And Buck of Buck and Bubbles was in the band and Austin Powell. I saw him today, you know, the guy that came up to the West End and sang "I Miss You So". He used to…

else. He played trumpet too. He could dance, play the piano. He was somethin'. He used to wake me up in the mornin' and play Louis Armstrong's solos note for note on the telephone at eight o'clock in the mornin'. I'm tellin' you, he was somethin'. But I worked with Timmy and I learned stage craft and we worked pretty good. We got down to Florida--and we were a little ahead of our time, just a little bit-- 'cause he had everything. But we got down to Florida and the Trenier Twins were the stars of the show. And…
